newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares pare some losses in IBIS dealings.
newsitem.headline: German shares pare some losses in IBIS dealings.

text.p: German shares ended bourse dealings on Tuesday with modest losses as the market took a small breather from sharp gains on Monday but still found some strength from the dollar trading above 1.79 marks.
The 30-share DAX ended the session down 3.06 points at 4,121.13 points, while the IBIS DAX was down 17.82 points at 4,124.37 points in post-bourse activity.
The IBIS DAX recovered in post-bourse computer dealings to end down 2.51 points at 4,139.68 points.

"The market was a bit disappointing in that many people expected further gains," said one Frankfurt trader. "The DAX needs to take a break, a pause. But this is not the start of some consolidation phase or a correction."
Dealers predicted the DAX would stabilise between 4,100 and 4,150 points in the coming days and be influenced by the dollar's movements and Wall Street.
The dollar's brief drop from Monday's highs, caused by German Finance Minister Theo Waigel saying on Tuesday that forex markets were overreacting, weighed on the market in morning dealings.
A decline in DAX heavyweight Allianz AG, which fell 13 marks to 420 marks, was one reason cited for the small losses.
But the dollar recovered to trade above 1.79 marks and gave renewed strength to the DAX since many of its components are industrial corporations strongly dependent on exports.
Chemical shares led the gains as Hoechst AG surged 1.40 marks to 81.40 marks, BASF AG rose 85 pfennigs to 68.40 marks and Bayer AG rose 15 pfennigs at 74.00 marks.

"There is no sign that the chemical sector has given up its rally," said one dealer. "We could be seeing some new record highs in these stocks this week and history shows that fresh record highs in the past has led to significant gains."

Carmaker Volkswagen AG, which, has been leading the DAX advance, was lower, falling 13.50 marks to 1,467.50 marks on profit-taking. Another top carmaker, Porsche AG, ended down 180 marks at 2,750 marks.
BMW AG set a new record at 1,544 marks but later suffered from profit-taking to end down four marks at 1,535 marks.
